encounters.cc: Daughter reports patient has become withdrawn with difficulty hearing conversations

lines: Daughter reports patient has become withdrawn with difficulty hearing conversations

This 66-year-old male with hypertension, congestive heart failure, hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis, and history of resolved pulmonary tuberculosis presents for Otolaryngology evaluation of hearing concerns.
His daughter has noticed that he often does not respond when she calls him from another room and seems to be watching television with the volume much higher than before.
The patient admits to feeling frustrated with his difficulty in following conversations, especially in noisy environments, and has started to avoid social gatherings.
- History of pulmonary tuberculosis (resolved, treated 20 years ago)
His past medical history includes hypertension, for which he takes hydrochlorothiazide.
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 10 years ago.
He denies any otalgia, otorrhea, or vertigo.
On physical examination, the patient has a normal otoscopic exam, and the whispered voice test reveals a decreased ability to hear whispered phrases bilaterally.
Tuning fork tests (Rinne and Weber) are unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Persistent cough and unexplained weight loss over three months

lines: Persistent cough and unexplained weight loss over three months
The patient is a 68-year-old male with hypertension and a history of bladder urothelial carcinoma.
He presents to the clinic with a persistent cough and unexplained weight loss over the past 3 months.
He denies any fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis.
- History of pulmonary tuberculosis (resolved, treated 20 years ago)
His past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide, and a remote history of tuberculosis treated 20 years ago.
On physical examination, he appears cachectic.
Lung auscultation reveals decreased breath sounds in the right upper lobe.
A chest X-ray shows a right upper lobe mass, and a CT scan confirms a 4 cm spiculated mass with no evidence of metastasis.

lines: Sudden painless loss of vision in right eye lasting 10 minutes, two hours ago

The patient is a 69-year-old male with congestive heart failure, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia who presented four months ago with acute decompensated heart failure, and now comes to the physician 2 hours after he experienced a 10-minute episode of sudden, painless loss of vision in his right eye.
He currently has no symptoms but the episode was extremely concerning and worrisome for him.
- Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
- History of pulmonary tuberculosis (resolved, treated 20 years ago)
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 10 years ago.
The patient is a 70-year-old male with congestive heart failure, non-small cell lung cancer, bladder urothelial carcinoma, and carotid artery stenosis, returning for routine follow-up.
He is usually punctual and cooperative at visits.
Today, however, he appears visibly frustrated and curt in his responses.
As the medical assistant begins the intake, the patient mutters that the waiting room was "a disaster," and complains loudly that he had to wait for over 30 minutes.
When the physician enters the room and greets him, the patient interrupts: "I'm sick of this! Every time I come here, I wait forever.
I'm not some nobody you can just ignore!" He crosses his arms and avoids eye contact, clearly agitated.
- Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
